headline: Pads Are On, Myths Are Off: St. Joe Is Where the 6-11 Hangover Ends
dek: After a nightmare 2025, camp battles at tackle, linebacker, and the interior DL will decide whether Mahomes gets a real identity—or another season of duct tape—by Week 1.
videoHook: Forget the 6-11 tape for a second—watch Josh Simmons jump a weight class, Peter Woods wreck the pocket like a pitbull, and tell me this defense still has a speed problem it refuses to fix.
theEdge: A strong camp that locks Simmons at LT, settles RT, and puts real juice next to Chris Jones is the only path from a 6.7% title market back to September relevance.

storyline.lede: Kansas City is back in St. Joseph with something it has not carried into camp in over a decade: a losing record and no participation trophies. The 6-11 collapse was not a blip the locker room pretends was fake—Trent McDuffie’s comments captured the shock—but Andy Reid’s staff is treating Missouri Western like a reset lab. Installs matter more than vibes. The offensive line must give Patrick Mahomes a clean pocket and a downhill run game; Steve Spagnuolo needs linebacker speed he has chased for years; and the skill room has to prove Brett Veach was right to largely run it back instead of chasing shiny wideout trades.
body: The clearest structural win so far is on the left edge. Josh Simmons is up a weight class and already penciled in as the Week 1 left tackle after an eight-game audition that put him on NFL.com’s All-Under 25 team. That stability is huge for Eric Bieniemy’s early-down menu—inside zone, play-action boots, and max-protect shots all start with a LT who can stone the edge. The problem is the other side: the right tackle competition is forcing a real Week 1 decision, and every rep in the wet grass at MWSU is audition tape, not depth-chart theater.

Defensively, the headline is dual-track. Rookie DT Peter Woods—the 29th pick out of Clemson—has veterans like Khyiris Tonga calling him a “little pitbull” through the first padded practices, which is exactly the interior disruption Spagnuolo needs beside Chris Jones. But the long-running linebacker speed question has not vanished; if camp does not produce a second-level answer, Cover-2 shells and simulated pressures will keep springing leaks in space the way they did during the 2025 freefall.

Rashee Rice is the skill player with the most to prove and the most encouraging early noise, while Kristian Fulton has missed again—another reminder that the secondary cannot assume full health into September. Emari Demarcado is carving the classic undrafted niche (protection, scouts, finish), and Cooper McDonald is talking like a second-year defender who finally sees a real snap path. None of that is chrome; it is roster math.

Look ahead, not backward. Polymarket has the Chiefs at 9.5% to win the AFC and 6.7% to hoist the Lombardi in 2027 pricing—honest underdog numbers after a lost year, not a dynasty default. What a strong camp unlocks is simple: a defined OL, a DL that can win early downs without blitzing every snap, and enough LB athleticism for Spagnuolo to call his full menu in Week 1. Fail those battles in St. Joe and the schedule will not care about the Arrowhead name going back on the building.

spotlight.title: Josh Simmons is the camp constant
spotlight.body: Simmons has jumped a weight class and is treated as the Week 1 left tackle after flashing across eight games a year ago. That lets Bieniemy script under-center zone and boots without protecting a soft edge first. His All-Under 25 nod is nice; finishing camp clean is the real deliverable.

spotlight.title: Right tackle is the Week 1 decision nobody can fake
spotlight.body: With Simmons set on the left, the right side is a live competition creating a difficult Week 1 call. Whichever body wins must hold up in both inside zone and seven-man protections or Mahomes will be back to backyard rules by October.

spotlight.title: Peter Woods is already moving grown men
spotlight.body: Through the first padded days, Woods has drawn “little pitbull” praise from Khyiris Tonga and looked like a star-in-the-making interior piece. Pairing that with Chris Jones is how Spagnuolo gets negative plays without selling out every down.

spotlight.title: The same linebacker question still shapes the defense
spotlight.body: Kansas City has chased second-level speed for years; camp is the latest referendum. If the LBs cannot run, Cover-2 turns into catch-and-run football and zone blitzes leave voids that good QBs will punish in Week 1.

spotlight.title: Rice has the most to prove—and the noise is positive
spotlight.body: The Associated Press tabbed Rashee Rice as the Chiefs player with the most to prove, and early camp reports have been encouraging even as the room largely ran it back. Chasing a Calvin Ridley rebound is a distraction Veach should keep ignoring.

spotlight.title: Demarcado and McDonald fighting for real roles
spotlight.body: Emari Demarcado is embracing the undrafted niche—protection, scout-team detail, finish—while Cooper McDonald says he is ready for the opportunity he has chased into Year 2. Those are the edges that decide 53-man cuts and early-down packages.

spotlight.title: Just Arrowhead again
spotlight.body: The club and G.E.H.A. are returning the plain Arrowhead Stadium branding for 2026—a small cultural reset that matches the on-field strip-down after 6-11. The building gets its name back; the roster still has to earn the noise.

xsandos.title: Under-Center Inside Zone — Simmons Seals the Edge
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, early script, Week 1 identity snaps when defenses load the box to test the new OL
xsandos.why: With Josh Simmons locked at LT and up a weight class, Bieniemy can finally call true downhill zone without the left edge collapsing. A settled (or at least decided) RT lets the center/guards work double-to-linebacker while Emari Demarcado or the lead back press the landmark—exactly the early-down tax the 6-11 offense stopped collecting.
xsandos.coaching: Simmons’ first step and anchor have to finish the reach; backs one-cut on the play-side hip—no east-west freelancing that recreated last year’s second-and-long death spiral.

xsandos.title: Play-Action Boot After Zone Look
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-medium following a successful inside-zone series; move Mahomes off the spot vs. aggressive Week 1 ends
xsandos.why: Simmons’ LT stability sells the fake; boot gets Patrick Mahomes on the perimeter with easy high-low reads and protects whatever RT wins the camp job from pure speed rushes. Rice working back across the formation is the prove-it touch Mahomes needs if the static WR room is truly enough.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes holds the fake one full count—Spagnuolo’s own camp scout looks will jump run. TE hinge must wall the DE; if the RT is still green, tight end chip rules are non-negotiable.

xsandos.title: Mesh vs. Man — Rice as the Rub Winner
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 3rd-and-7, two-minute or early third-down sets against press-man looks Week 1
xsandos.why: AP flagged Rashee Rice as the Chiefs skill player with the most to prove; mesh puts him on a natural rub crosser where YAC and toughness show up without needing a new vertical burner. Avoiding a Calvin Ridley distraction only works if this room wins man-coverage downs in September.
xsandos.coaching: Rice must attack the contact and finish through the tangle—no polite paths. Back checkdown (Demarcado niche) is live if both crossers get trailed; Mahomes throws on time or the mesh dies.

xsandos.title: RB Screen — Easy Offense When the Pass Rush Climbs
xsandos.situation: Early downs or empty protections when opposing fronts pin their ears back at Mahomes after 2025 tape study
xsandos.why: A rebuilt interior with Woods and Jones will draw extra attention; the screen punishes that aggression and keeps Mahomes from living in collapsed pockets while the RT battle is still settling. Demarcado’s “niche” value is exactly this: set up, release clean, finish in space.
xsandos.coaching: Guards and center must get to the second level flat—no wasted vertical steps. Back sells pass pro for a full beat; Mahomes’ eyes stay downfield until the throw window, not a panic dump.

xsandos.title: Spagnuolo Cover-2 Shell — Protect the LB Speed Gap
xsandos.situation: Long-yardage and obvious passing downs Week 1 while the linebacker athleticism question is still live
xsandos.why: If camp does not fully solve the multi-year LB speed issue, Cover-2 is the honest answer: two deep take away the shot, five under rally, and Jones/Woods win the interior so the second level is tackling, not chasing vertically. McDuffie’s standard on the outside only works if the shell is disciplined behind him—especially with Fulton missing practice time.
xsandos.coaching: Corners squat and funnel; safeties split the posts, no freelancing. LBs must expand then collapse—Cooper McDonald’s Year-2 opportunity shows up here as a run-fit and shallow-cross robber, not a highlight blitzer.

xsandos.title: Simulated Pressure — Woods as the Pitbull Piece
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7 to 3rd-and-5, neutral script when Spagnuolo wants a negative play without true all-out heat
xsandos.why: Peter Woods’ early padded-practice violence lets Spagnuolo show five or six and still drop a lineman into the hole—signature simulated pressure that stressed QBs when healthy. Pairing Woods’ interior burst with Jones means the “blitz” can be a mirage that still wins the A-gap while covering the LB speed limitation in behind zones.
xsandos.coaching: Pre-snap crowd the LOS, post-snap exchange clean—Woods either wins the one-on-one or occupies two so the second-level rusher is free. Dropping end must replace the hook; missed exchanges are how 2025 turned pressures into chunk plays.

coaching.detail: Camp must reinstall under-center zone and boot as the spine so Mahomes is not stuck in empty shotgun guesswork by Week 1. Simmons at LT is the green light; the RT winner is the red light if he cannot finish zone steps.
The linebacker speed question still shapes call-sheet aggression. Until that room proves it in pads, expect more Cover-2 shells and simulated pressures that hide athletic gaps behind Jones and Woods.

Running back the WR room and ignoring Ridley-trade noise only looks smart if Rice’s prove-it camp turns into September separation. Niche contributors like Demarcado are how a 6-11 roster finds hidden snaps without splash signings.

Weather-impacted days moving indoors then back to wet grass at Missouri Western are lengthening practices and stress-testing conditioning—Reid’s injury updates after those sessions are as important as the depth chart graphics.

strategies: Script under-center inside zone behind Simmons in Week 1 to reestablish early-down leverage lost in 2025.
Pair every zone series with a boot or naked off the same look so defenses cannot key run when the RT is still proving it.
Feature Rice on mesh and shallow crossers early to settle the prove-it narrative without needing a new vertical acquisition.
Deploy Woods-Jones interior twists on early downs so Spagnuolo can play cleaner coverage behind them.
Default to Cover-2 and simulated pressures until a true LB speed answer wins the camp reps.
Use Demarcado on protection-first packages and screens to keep Mahomes clean while OL chemistry finishes cooking.
Resist splash WR trades; force the current room to win camp 1-on-1s and let the market’s 6.7% title price be earned back on the field.
debates: Is the RT competition close enough that KC should open Week 1 in heavier 12 personnel to hide it?
Can Peter Woods be a three-down rookie, or is he an early-down wrecker only next to Chris Jones?
Did Veach make the right call running back the WR room, or will September expose the lack of a Ridley-level separator?
Which linebacker actually solves the speed problem—or is Spagnuolo scheming around a hole that never closes?
Should Mahomes’ camp rep count be managed like a rehab ramp even if he is listed full, given the 2025 workload hangover narrative?
Does going back to plain “Arrowhead Stadium” branding signal a real cultural reset—or just cleaner signage on a 6-11 rebuild year?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Hit the Defector-style takedown energy without wallowing: the nightmare was real, McDuffie said they never believed it, and camp is the first honest work since. Tease Simmons weight jump and Woods pitbull clips.
Put Polymarket on screen: 9.5% AFC, 6.7% champion. Not disrespect—pricing after 6-11. Frame what camp must unlock to move those numbers by October.

runOfShow.segment: OL board — Simmons locked, RT chaos
runOfShow.talkTrack: Film-room on Simmons as Week 1 LT and All-Under 25 pedigree. Break down why the right tackle competition is the hardest decision and how it changes zone/boot installs.

runOfShow.segment: Defense — Woods juice vs. LB speed hole
runOfShow.talkTrack: Tonga’s pitbull line on Woods, Jones as the still-elite anchor, then the multi-year linebacker speed question that shapes every Spagnuolo call. Cover-2 and zone-blitz as the honest bridge.
Rice prove-it arc and encouraging reports; why Ridley trade talk is noise; Demarcado niche; McDonald’s Year-2 shot. Fulton misses as the secondary caution.
Walk the six concepts—inside zone, boot, mesh, screen, Cover-2, zone blitz—tied to named camp winners and holes. Whiteboard only; no generic playbook filler.
Pose the RT/personnel questions, title-market honesty, and what a clean final week of camp means for Week 1 call sheets. Close on Arrowhead name restoration as vibe, not substance.
